issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently refers to the animal feeding method using two different names: it defines an abstract method messageOnFeed() for Animal (and the UML shows messageOnFeed()), but later task descriptions and the song template refer to getFeedingSound(). The template Farm.java uses TODOs and a commented-out animal parameter, and the solution implements and uses messageOnFeed(). This name inconsistency in the specification (messageOnFeed vs getFeedingSound) can confuse students about which method to implement and call when feeding animals and when printing the song.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent by using a single method name for the animal feeding sound across the problem statement, UML, template and tests. Preferably update the problem statement (and any examples) to consistently use messageOnFeed() everywhere (or change the solution/template to use getFeedingSound()), and update the song template text to call that same method. Ensure template Farm.java includes the correct parameter and calls the consistent method name so students know which method to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement's task descriptions refer to a method named getFeedingSound() for animal feeding sounds, while the UML, template intent, and the solution implementation use the method name messageOnFeed(). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (obtaining the animal's feeding sound) can confuse students about which method to implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Update the problem statement to reference messageOnFeed() (preferred, matching the UML and solution) everywhere getFeedingSound() appears — or alternatively provide getFeedingSound() as a clear alias in the template/solution. Prefer using messageOnFeed() in instructions so students implement the same identifier as in provided code.
